Subject: Data residency requirements for upcoming procurement - FinServ RFP

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the call earlier. As we prepare the formal RFP response, procurement has asked for a concise matrix that confirms:
- Whether customer data can be resident in EU-only regions (data at rest and logs).
- Where the control plane/management console lives and whether it can be located outside EU.
- Options for KMS/HSM key storage (customer-managed keys by region).
- Fallback behavior when primary EU capacity is constrained (does data move, is processing denied, or is there an opt-in routing to another region?).
- Audit log locations and retention controls.

Can you share a short operational playbook and a matrix by 2026-07-12 so we can include it in the procurement package? Also note procurement will require a short paragraph we can include in the contract about guaranteed regional placement and any exceptions.

Hi Lucia — thanks, we can do that. I attached a first-pass matrix that maps our deployment and controls to the items you listed. Highlights up front:
- EU-resident data: supported via Dedicated and Private deployments; hosted API supports EU-only tenancy when requested (see matrix rows).
- Control plane: default hosted control plane is multi-region; Private customers can run control plane in their VPC.
- KMS/HSM: customer-managed KMS with region-scoped keys is supported for Private; hosted offers KMS integration and can pin key residency.
- Fallback: we offer configurable routing policies — options are deny, replicate to another pinned region (with explicit consent), or route to a compatibility model in a non-EU region with redaction flags.

Please see attached: 20260701-residency-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet) and a short playbook we will expand. I'll loop in engineering and security to tighten the wording before 7/12.

Folks — draft technical language below (feel free to copy/paste into the playbook). I also attached an updated residency matrix with column-level detail for logs, keys, and model artifacts.

A. Definitions (copy-ready):
- "EU-resident customer data": customer-provided inputs, generated outputs, and metadata persisted in storage that are written to a storage tier physically located within an EU region selected at onboarding.
- "Control plane": service management endpoints (API, console) that may be hosted outside the EU for hosted customers; for Private deployments, control plane can be provisioned in-customer VPC (EU region) upon request.

B. Deployment & guarantees:
- Hosted (default): Customer data storage can be pinned to EU regions; control plane is global by default but may be restricted via Private offer. Audit logs for hosted customers are stored in region of record; retention configurable but short-term trace logs are replicated for reliability (replicas are tagged and access-controlled).
- Dedicated / Private: Full EU residency for data, logs, and keys. Customer-managed KMS/HSM supported; Redwood will not have access to customer-managed keys.

C. KMS/HSM specifics:
- Hosted: Redwood integrates with customer KMS providers (KMS calls proxied); key material is stored per the KMS vendor region. We can accept a contractual requirement to keep keys in EU for EU-residency customers.
- Private: You hold keys in your KMS/HSM; we provide integration guidance and an operational checklist for key rotation and audits.

D. Fallback strategies (ordered):
1) Soft-deny + queuing: if EU capacity is saturated, requests are queued for configurable time (customer sets time-to-wait) and not routed out of region.
2) Explicit opt-in cross-region routing: with documented consent, traffic can be routed to a secondary region (US/APAC) to complete processing; data is tagged and access controls applied.
3) Model-variant routing (latency-first): route to an equivalent, lower-capacity model hosted in EU-friendly compatible infra; no data egress.
4) Emergency regional failover: with prior contractual agreement, replicate operational state to a pre-approved non-EU region for defined duration (requires DocuSign SLA exception).

E. Logs & audit:
- Audit logs for data access are retained in-region by default; customers can request longer retention or cross-region replication for analytics (explicit opt-in).
- We provide regular SOC2-aligned attestations and a read-only audit export that can be pushed to customer S3/GCS in a pinned region.

Operational notes (Jonas): onboarding to pin an EU region typically takes 5-10 business days for Dedicated; Private onboarding varies by network setup. See matrix for exact timelines.

Attachment: updated matrix: 20260706-residency-matrix-updated.xlsx

-Karthik
Staff Software Engineer, Inference Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

Subject: Regional residency playbook + contract paragraph (FinServ RFP)

Hi Lucia — attached is the finalized playbook and the short contract paragraph for procurement. Key excerpts below for quick review: 

Contract paragraph (suggested):
"Redwood Inference will store Customer Data (inputs, outputs, and persistent metadata) within the EU region selected at onboarding. The control plane may be hosted outside the EU for Hosted customers; customers electing Private or Dedicated deployment models may request the control plane be provisioned within their EU region. Cross-region processing or temporary replication will only occur with Customer's prior written consent or per an executed SLA exception. KMS keys used for encryption at rest will be maintained in the Customer-specified region where Customer provides or configures regional key management."

Operational summary (one-line bullets):
- EU-resident data: supported via Dedicated and Private; hosted tenancy supports region pinning.
- Default fallback: soft-deny + queuing (configurable) to avoid involuntary egress.
- Opt-in fallback: explicit cross-region routing or documented emergency failover (requires SLA exception).
- KMS: customer-managed keys supported; we will integrate with region-scoped keys.

Attachments: RFP-Response-FinServ-Redwood-20260712.pdf (playbook) and 20260701-residency-matrix.xlsx (detailed matrix).

Please confirm if procurement would like the SLA exception draft now — I can route it for DocuSign. Suggested next step: procurement approves paragraph and we add the SLA exception as an appendix to the agreement.
